documents.unit: one approved knowledge entry equals one chunk

lexical_floor.tokenizer: baseline tokenizer: NFKC + casefold; ASCII alphanumeric tokens with lightweight English stemming; each contiguous Chinese sequence plus overlapping Chinese bigrams; no jieba or word segmenter

reporting.per_plant_use: failure detection only; never model selection or superiority claims

diagnostic_amendment_before_embedding_ru.reason: The true content-only BM25 run showed that zero-score ties can fill Top-K and create accidental gold hits.
report_both: forced Top-K using the baseline deterministic entry-ID tie-break
signal-only BM25 retaining candidates with score > 0
diagnostic_amendment_before_embedding_ru.numeric_guard: Embeddings are checked for finite values; similarity uses normalized embeddings with deterministic float64 einsum after NumPy matmul emitted spurious overflow warnings despite finite inputs and outputs.

runtime.similarity: cosine via normalized embeddings and deterministic float64 einsum

notes: Content-only BM25 and dense retrieval use only entry.content and no entity or dimension filters.
Forced Top-K retains zero-score BM25 ties; positive-score-only isolates observed lexical signal.
Every approved knowledge entry is one chunk; no secondary splitting is applied.
Per-plant metrics are diagnostic only because dev plant counts are too small for model comparison.
The lexical-overlap count 4/91 and semantic Top-K pair recall are different metrics and are not placed on one numeric scale.
